outline.chapter_title: Mathematical Reasoning with LLMs: Context, Benchmarks, and Goals
outline.description: This chapter motivates mathematical reasoning as a core challenge for language models, surveys key benchmarks and reasoning paradigms, and positions DeepSeekMath within the landscape of open and closed systems. It sets expectations, clarifies evaluation protocols, and introduces the paper’s main contributions and claims.
subtopics: Why mathematical reasoning is difficult for LLMs: structure, precision, long-range dependencies
Benchmark landscape: GSM8K, MATH, SAT, OCW Courses, MMLU-STEM, MGSM-zh, CMATH, Gaokao-MathCloze, Gaokao-MathQA, miniF2F
Reasoning paradigms: Chain-of-Thought (CoT), Program-of-Thought (PoT), tool-integrated reasoning, formal theorem proving
Open vs closed models: performance gap and accessibility (GPT-4, Gemini-Ultra/Pro, Minerva) vs open-source models
DeepSeekMath overview: goals, components (Corpus, Base, Instruct, RL), headline results (e.g., 51.7% MATH without tools; 60.9% self-consistency on MATH)
Evaluation protocols: self-contained text solutions vs program-based solutions; few-shot prompting; self-consistency voting
Decontamination ethics and methodology: preventing benchmark leakage in pre-training data
Prerequisites refresher for readers: probability and optimization basics, supervised vs reinforcement learning, PPO at a glance

outline.chapter_title: Building the DeepSeekMath Corpus and Base Model
outline.description: This chapter explains how a large, high-quality math corpus was constructed from Common Crawl and how it powers a strong base model. It covers the iterative data mining pipeline, decontamination, multilinguality, quality validation against other corpora, and the training and evaluation of DeepSeekMath-Base 7B, including transfer to general reasoning and code.
subtopics: Data sourcing from Common Crawl: deduplication (URL-based and near-duplicate removal), scale considerations
fastText classifier pipeline: seed with OpenWebMath; positive/negative sampling; key hyperparameters; iterative improvement
Iterative mining and curation: domain grouping, math-related domain discovery, manual URL annotation, four iterations; outcome (35.5M pages; 120B tokens)
Ranking and thresholding: token budgets (40B, 80B, 120B, 160B) and selection strategy
Decontamination: 10-gram and exact-match filtering against English and Chinese benchmarks
Corpus properties and comparisons: scale, multilingual coverage (notably Chinese), vs MathPile, OpenWebMath, Proof-Pile-2
Quality validation with a 1.3B model: training setup (optimizer, schedule, batch, context), learning curves, downstream results

Pretraining DeepSeekMath-Base 7B: initialization from DeepSeek-Coder-Base-v1.5; 500B tokens; data mix (56% DeepSeekMath, 4% AlgebraicStack, 10% arXiv, 20% GitHub code, 10% CC NL EN/ZH); optimizer and schedule
Performance without tools: strong results across GSM8K, MATH, CMATH, MMLU-STEM; surpassing open-source baselines and Minerva 540B on MATH
Program-aided reasoning with PoT: Python and sympy execution; improvements over prior SOTA (e.g., Llemma-34B)
Formal mathematics: miniF2F autoformalization with Isabelle and Sledgehammer; few-shot proof sketching pipeline
Generalization beyond math: gains on MMLU, BBH; retention of coding ability on HumanEval and MBPP

Empirical findings and ablations: code training benefits mathematical reasoning (with and without tools); two-stage vs one-stage training; catastrophic forgetting and mixing; limited impact of arXiv-only corpora and caveats

outline.description: This chapter details the supervised fine-tuning (SFT) stage that adapts the base model for step-by-step and tool-integrated mathematical problem solving. It covers dataset construction, multilingual coverage, training recipes, evaluation with and without tools, and practical lessons for building strong instruction-tuned math models.
subtopics: SFT dataset construction: 776K examples; English and Chinese coverage; CoT, PoT, and tool-integrated formats
English sources and annotations: GSM8K, MATH with tool-integrated solutions; MathInstruct subset; Lila-OOD; topic diversity
Chinese sources and annotations: K-12 problems across 76 sub-topics with CoT and tool-integrated solutions
Training recipe: concatenation up to 4K context; 500 steps; batch size 256; learning rate 5e-5
Evaluation without tools: DeepSeekMath-Instruct 7B vs open/closed models; strong MATH performance approaching larger proprietary models
Evaluation with tools: approaching 60% on MATH via Python execution; competitiveness with much larger open models
Prompting and decoding considerations: few-shot CoT, PoT prompts; self-consistency strategies
Observed effects: multilingual benefits; transfer to reasoning and coding; comparison to math-focused instruction-tuned baselines
Practical failure modes and mitigations: error types, robustness, and data diversity

outline.chapter_title: Reinforcement Learning with Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO)
outline.description: This chapter presents GRPO, an efficient PPO variant that improves mathematical reasoning without a critic model by leveraging group-relative baselines. It develops the math, contrasts with PPO and other alignment methods, details outcome vs process supervision and iterative training, reports empirical gains, and distills insights on why RL helps and how to make it more effective.
subtopics: Motivation for RL after SFT: remaining gaps and PPO limitations (critic overhead, token-level reward sparsity)
PPO refresher: actor-critic, GAE, per-token KL regularization; practical memory and stability issues
GRPO objective and training dynamics: group sampling, relative baseline from group scores, no critic; KL regularization via unbiased estimator; resource efficiency
Outcome vs process supervision in GRPO: reward placement and advantage computation; step-aware rewards
Iterative GRPO: updating reward models with replay and resetting references; stability and performance considerations

Training DeepSeekMath-RL 7B: data scope (144K CoT questions from GSM8K/MATH), reward model training, key hyperparameters (e.g., lr 1e-6, KL 0.04, group size 64, max length 1024, batch 1024), single update per exploration
Results: GSM8K 88.2%, MATH 51.7% without tools; out-of-domain gains (e.g., CMATH); self-consistency 60.9% on MATH
Unified paradigm of SFT, RFT, DPO, PPO, GRPO: data source (online vs offline), reward function (rule vs model), gradient coefficient design and implications
Empirical analyses: Online RFT vs RFT; GRPO vs Online RFT; process vs outcome supervision; iterative RL boosts
Why RL works: Maj@K vs Pass@K analysis; distributional robustness vs fundamental capability

Limitations and future directions: reward generalization and uncertainty, weak-to-strong alignment, advanced decoding and search, efficient inference, geometry and proof gaps, few-shot limitations, data selection refinements
